runs.title: Ashley Moody and the silicosis story

runs.answer: The New Republic piece (Kate Aronoff, Oct. 23, 2026) profiles Tampa-area stone fabricator Wade Hanicker, 39, whose silicosis from cutting engineered-stone countertops left him with a ~$100,000 bill and joined him to the hundreds of workers suing manufacturers; it cites California's 668 confirmed engineered-stone silicosis cases and 35 deaths since 2019 (3,000 expected by 2030), notes California's pending emergency ban and Australia's 2024 quartz ban, and accuses Sen. Ashley Moody — "up for reelection next month" — of sponsoring S.4792, the "Protection of Lawful Commerce in Stone Slab Products Act of 2026," to give stone-slab makers lawsuit immunity akin to gun and vaccine manufacturers, after her campaign and Victory Fund took $38,000 from the family of Cambria CEO Marty Davis. I verified the bill's text on GovInfo: S.4792 (119th Congress, introduced June 16, 2026) would bar "qualified civil actions" over silica exposure from third-party fabrication of stone slab products in state and federal court and require dismissal of pending suits. Ashley Moody is the Republican U.S. Senator from Florida, appointed in January 2025 to Marco Rubio's seat after serving as Florida attorney genera
